interface.title: Image Segmentation & Particle Analysis (Segmentation Studio, SEM/TEM particle workflow, v2.0)
interface.field: Electron microscopy / nanomaterials characterization (particle size distribution analysis)
interface.stage_of_work: Image analysis and quantification, from raw micrographs to exported size statistics
interface.what_it_is_for: Segment particles in SEM/TEM micrographs with a pretrained neural model, measure each particle in nanometres, show the size distributions, and export the measurements as CSV/ZIP.

data.note: I uploaded coins.png (384×303) and nuclei-fluorescence.png through 'Upload files'. Folder mode with /work/app/assets returned 'No images found in the specified folder'. The model was the stock COCO-trained YOLOv8n-seg from /work/app/Models. With CLAHE (clip 3.0) and ×2 rebinning it found 0 particles. With no preprocessing it found 3 coins in coins.png and 0 in nuclei-fluorescence.png. With a 35 nm minimum size it found 2. These counts reflect the general-purpose model, not the tool. Pixel size stayed at the default 0.719 nm/px, so every nm value in this run comes from that default.

tree.general: Turn microscopy images of many small objects into per-object size measurements and size distributions in physical units, ready for reporting
tree.specific: Segment particles in SEM/TEM micrographs with a pretrained model (the tool supports SAM, SAM2, MobileSAM, FastSAM and YOLOv8; this run used YOLOv8n-seg), review masks/crops/measurements, inspect nm size distributions, and export CSV/ZIP

Setting the image scale (Pixel size, nm/px) so measurements come out in physical units: a core step that every nm value, crop label, histogram and export depends on, but it stayed at the default 0.719 nm/px and was never changed before the ~100-action budget ran out
Device options other than cpu (CUDA/MPS): I didn't open the dropdown; there is no GPU here anyway
Max size value filter and other Size metric choices: I only tested Min size = 35 nm
Particle Crops 'Max particles to display' slider: I saw it but didn't drag it (only 3 particles)
Fullscreen on the mask overlay and figures, and the table's Search/Fullscreen/CSV toolbar buttons: not tried
I didn't inspect the ZIP's contents: browser_read_download reports binary files by size only (1,788,805 bytes)

Segmentation of nuclei-fluorescence.png: 0 particles every time. This is a limit of the general COCO-trained model, not a broken pipeline. The whole chain (segment → results → distributions → export) did run end to end on coins.png on CPU
